sn22.94:1.2: “Bhikkhus, I do not dispute with the world; rather, it is the world that disputes with me.
sn22.94:1.3: A proponent of the Dhamma does not dispute with anyone in the world.
sn22.94:1.4: Of that which the wise in the world agree upon as not existing, I too say that it does not exist.
sn22.94:1.5: And of that which the wise in the world agree upon as existing, I too say that it exists.
sn22.94:2.1: “And what is it, bhikkhus, that the wise in the world agree upon as not existing, of which I too say that it does not exist?
sn22.94:2.2: Form that is permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change: this the wise in the world agree upon as not existing, and I too say that it does not exist.
sn22.94:2.6: Consciousness that is permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change: this the wise in the world agree upon as not existing, and I too say that it does not exist.
sn22.94:2.7: “That, bhikkhus, is what the wise in the world agree upon as not existing, of which I too say that it does not exist.
sn22.94:3.1: “And what is it, bhikkhus, that the wise in the world agree upon as existing, of which I too say that it exists?
sn22.94:3.2: Form that is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change: this the wise in the world agree upon as existing, and I too say that it exists.
sn22.94:3.4: Consciousness that is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change: this the wise in the world agree upon as existing, and I too say that it exists.
sn22.94:3.5: “That, bhikkhus, is what the wise in the world agree upon as existing, of which I too say that it exists.
sn22.94:4.1: “There is, bhikkhus, a world-phenomenon in the world to which the Tathagata has awakened and broken through.
sn22.94:4.2: Having done so, he explains it, teaches it, proclaims it, establishes it, discloses it, analyses it, elucidates it.
sn22.94:5.1: “And what is that world-phenomenon in the world to which the Tathagata has awakened and broken through?
sn22.94:5.2: Form, bhikkhus, is a world-phenomenon in the world to which the Tathagata has awakened and broken through.
sn22.94:5.3: Having done so, he explains it, teaches it, proclaims it, establishes it, discloses it, analyses it, elucidates it.
sn22.94:6.1: When it is being thus explained … … and elucidated by the Tathagata, if anyone does not know and see, how can I do anything with that foolish worldling, blind and sightless, who does not know and does not see?
sn22.94:6.5: Consciousness is a world-phenomenon in the world to which the Tathagata has awakened and broken through.
sn22.94:6.6: Having done so, he explains it, teaches it, proclaims it, establishes it, discloses it, analyses it, elucidates it.
sn22.94:7.1: When it is being thus explained … and elucidated by the Tathagata, if anyone does not know and see, how can I do anything with that foolish worldling, blind and sightless, who does not know and does not see?
sn22.94:8.1: “Bhikkhus, just as a blue, red, or white lotus is born in the water and grows up in the water, but having risen up above the water, it stands unsullied by the water,
sn22.94:8.2: so too the Tathagata was born in the world and grew up in the world, but having overcome the world, he dwells unsullied by the world.”
